title: Scripture and Tradition
definition: Scripture and tradition must be rightly ordered: faithful traditions may serve the Church, but Scripture alone is the final authority over faith and practice.
summary: Tradition may serve the Church, but it must remain under the authority of Scripture.
christFocus: Jesus rebuked traditions that nullified God's Word and called people back to God's commands.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Traditions can be helpful when they preserve faithful practice, teaching, and worship. But tradition becomes dangerous when it overrules, obscures, or replaces Scripture.

The believer must distinguish between God's commands and human customs. Scripture is the final authority that judges every tradition.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People can defend tradition simply because it is familiar. Scripture and tradition matters because inherited practice must always be tested by God's Word.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor what is faithful and helpful, but hold every tradition under Scripture. Be willing to change where God's Word corrects human practice.
